Let's infer from ADMM standard:
The code has methods `_mul_A(thing, over_relax)`, `_mul_B(thing, over_relax)`, `_add_C(thing, over_relax)`.
`_mul_A` overrelax:
```
if over_relax and A: alpha*A@thing
elif no A: alpha*thing
elif not overrelax and A: A@thing
return thing
```
`_mul_B`:
overrelax and B: (1-alpha)*B@thing
elif overrelax no B: -(1-alpha)*thing
not overrelax B: B@thing
else: -thing
```
`_add_C` ...
`get_X_step_bias` maybe returns `_mul_B(Z, over_relax?) + C`? `get_Z_step_bias` maybe `_mul_A(X)+C`.
From ADMM linearized update:
x^{k+1}=argmin f(x)+ rho/2 ||A x+B z^k - c + u^k||²
z^{k+1}=argmin g(z)+ rho/2 ||alpha A x^{k+1}+(1-alpha)B z^k - c + u^k||²
u^{k+1}=u^k+alpha A x^{k+1}+(1-alpha)B z^k - c
The linear term in x includes A^T(u+Bz-c); Z update B^T(...). 
`get_X_step_bias` perhaps `-A^T(BZ-c+u)` or `_mul_A(_dual_var_bias, False)` etc.
`get_Z_step_bias` perhaps `-B^T(AX-c+u)`.
`_dual_var_bias` maybe `u + A X + B Z - C`.
`update_dual_var` computes new u and primal/dual residuals dict, returns residual.
